text:
Ashley: who can bless a merge slot for https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6284? cc @runtime @platform @infra @security. This is the KV-prefetch + small allocator tweak that unblocks the canary pipeline. Need approvals and a deploy window — quick context below.

Mike: :eyes: I can review. what's the intended canary window and do we expect any perf regressions?

Ashley: planning the canary tomorrow 10:30am PT. Local CI shows ~+0.4% median latency; main risk is eviction thrash under high concurrency. Added tests: `eviction_smoke_test` and `kv-prefetch-e2e`.

Sara: Platform can take the scheduling if sec and infra sign off. If infra gives a thumbs, we can reserve the 10:30 slot. Need infra to confirm allocator change is safe in prod.

Leo: I can validate the allocator change. paste the config diff here and I'll run the perf job. Pinged the PR.

Ashley: here is the config diff snippet:
```
diff --git a/orch/allocator/config.yaml b/orch/allocator/config.yaml
@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@
 eviction:
   policy: lru
+  pinned_pool_size: 64
 kv:
   prefetch: true
```

Leo: thanks. quick sanity check: pinned_pool_size default is 32, bump to 64 seems fine. lgtm from infra if unit tests pass. I'll kick off the perf job now — ETA ~30m.

Jen: SEC question — does this touch any KMS/HSM or key access patterns? If not, I can approve after CI + perf pass. If yes, need a short security note.

Ashley: no KMS changes. purely in-memory allocator + config flag. CI is green except one flaky `io_timeout_test` (known flake, will follow up in separate PR). Perf job is running.

deploy-bot: Canary slot hold created for 10:30 PT tomorrow (us-west-2). Please update runbook if any special steps: https://docs/internal/runbooks/eviction-canary

Mike: reviewed the code; left one tiny nit but non-blocking. Approve from runtime side. :thumbsup:

Leo: perf job results: median +0.6%, p95 stable. infra approves for canary.

Jen: security approves — no new key access, no sensitive surface change.

Ashley: great, thanks everyone. I'll merge after resolving the one tiny nit and tag @release-coordinator for final handoff. :raised_hands:
